method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse reconstruction of the symbol inventory and examples, branch-by-branch review of conditional TeX, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: First-order language vocabulary; logical and non-logical symbol inventories; restricted example languages; primitive and defined notation; alternate symbols; and functional and expressive completeness.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: First-order languages build terms and formulas from variables, constants, predicates and sometimes functions, together with logical notation. Predicates name properties or relations, constants name individuals and functions name mappings; apart from identity these are the non-logical symbols that determine a language.
samples.checks: The four vocabulary classes, term/formula distinction, punctuation, identity exception, language-determination claim and unbounded general inventory are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The general inventory divides logical symbols, variables, non-logical predicates/constants/functions and punctuation. The standard language has denumerably many symbols of each indicated arity, although applications may restrict the non-logical stock.
samples.checks: Every connective, quantifier, truth constant, identity symbol, displayed indexed family, n-greater-than-zero condition and restriction clause remains in its original class.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Arithmetic uses less-than, zero, successor, addition and multiplication; set theory uses membership; order theory uses less-than-or-equal. These familiar marks are aliases for the indexed official symbols.
samples.checks: All arities and the exact alias mapping to A-zero-two, c-zero, f-zero-one, f-zero-two and f-one-two are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: When tags select them, additional connectives, quantifiers and truth constants are defined symbols. They abbreviate long primitive formulas and shorten proofs because every primitive symbol needs its own proof treatment.
samples.checks: All tag conditions and branch alternatives are unchanged, and the distinction between language membership and informal abbreviation remains explicit.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Logic uses many alternative marks and names for connectives and truth constants. Constants conventionally use early lowercase Latin letters, variables use later ones, and both quantifiers have several notational variants.
samples.checks: Each alternate symbol, terminology group, letter convention and universal/existential notation list is retained without reassignment.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A language may take all operators as primitive or define some from a smaller stock. Three displayed Boolean bases plus either quantifier yield an expressively complete first-order language; Sheffer stroke and Peirce arrow are individually truth-functionally complete under nand and nor readings.
samples.checks: The three operator sets, either-quantifier condition, named operators, eponyms, respective nand/nor readings and two distinct completeness notions are preserved.

source_observations: The target keeps identity among the logical symbols and predicates, constants and functions among the non-logical symbols.
The target distinguishes denumerability from arbitrary infinity and preserves every displayed arity.
Every conditional TeX tag, formula, macro, controlled token, identifier and reference matches exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The long terminology lists include conventional transliterations and provisional compounds flagged in the decision ledger for expert review.
The source treats its familiar mathematical symbols as aliases for a fixed indexed standard language; other presentations may take those symbols as primitive in their own signatures.
